docs: record §4.5.592 — 🆕 V reverted whole after three rounds: refusing or replaying a decision the walks disagree on each descends while later walks read the previous walk's binding; BLOCKED on the "Scoping" later-walk reads line and 🆕 AE

§4.5.592 was reverted whole and nothing of the attempt lands, so this
commit is its record. Oracles: iverilog 13.0 -g2012, verilator 5.052
--binary --timing, sv2v 0.0.13 -> iverilog.

- Bug (§2 🆕 V): each of the four GenPhase walks (`instance.rs` Nets,
  VarInit, Logic, Instances) re-runs `generate.rs` `elaborate_gen_item`
  (`GenItem::Case`, `elaborate_gen_if`, `GenItem::For`). A
  generate-scope parameter is bound at its position in every walk, is
  re-bound in every walk and is never unbound (`(_, ModuleItem::Param)`).
  So a walk after Nets reads the previous walk's inner binding of a
  parameter declared after the reference, where Nets read the outer
  object or none, and a forward reference mixes arms: nets from the
  Nets arm, processes and instances from a later one. V04x PRE
  `k 8 bits=6`, iverilog `one 1 bits=6`; I4 `then` / `else`; F3
  `L0 L1 L2` / `L0`; Z0c `local 8 bits=4` / `pkg 9 bits=4`; d1p
  `k 8 bits=4`, which iverilog refuses.
- Grounding discarded two cuts. A scope-wide decision view accepted 16
  designs iverilog refuses and sent F1 and Z1g loud -> silent-wrong
  (Z1g through 🆕 AE). Caching the Nets decision turned accidental
  louds into a silent default (AE7, V14b, V17, Z1d, Z1e). Built
  instead: record the Nets decision per construct instance (prefix,
  kind, span) and verify it in each later walk. Corpus and examples
  stayed byte-identical (.vu / .velab, every round) and elaboration
  time within ±3% (round 1); what failed was the policy for a mismatch.
- Three mismatch policies, one per review round; the mismatch axis drew
  BLOCKING in each round (LOOPROMPT §4, ER §3.6):
  1. E3010 on every mismatch (round 1) refuses legal designs PRE prints
     right: DL01, DL06, DL08 `@bits=4`, DL03 `@Q=10`, DL11
     `@w=9 bits=4`, all = iverilog.
  2. A silent replay where the Nets walk read every input, E3010 only
     for an unread label (round 2), exposes 🆕 AE: Z1g, PRE loud (an
     undeclared-net cascade), replay `L0 w=10 P=0000`, iverilog
     `L0 w=10 P=xxxx`.
  3. A silent replay where neither arm builds anything, E3010 otherwise
     (round 3). Every walk still re-binds the arm's parameters (SN6:
     iverilog, sv2v, verilator and PRE `P=1`, replay `P=9`). The replay
     drops the range report each walk makes (R3q: PRE and 3 oracles
     refuse `localparam [Nope:0] Q`, replay `@bits=4`). Its refusal
     half still refuses R3a, R3b and R3m, where PRE = iverilog.
- Mechanism of the failure: the walks disagree because they read
  different bindings. Refusing the mismatch catches legal designs whose
  arms print alike. Replaying the Nets decision leaves every later
  walk's other reads (the arm's parameters, its range reports, the
  interpreter's 0) on the later binding. Root fix: bind each generate
  level's own parameters by position in every walk after Nets (restore
  the level's own keys at its entry), so the walks agree by
  construction. A decision that fix moves can reach 🆕 AE's 0 (Z1g).
- Oracle ruling (kept; it outlives the revert): IEEE 1800-2017 §26.3
  decides forward references in a generate scope. A reference other
  than a call binds a declaration before it, else in the next outer
  scope, else it is illegal (Example 1). iverilog follows it. sv2v and
  verilator bind scope-wide and contradict the example (Z0a: iverilog
  `px=1 bx=2`, sv2v `px=z bx=2`, verilator `px=0 bx=2`), so they are
  disqualified on this axis. It is recorded in ROADMAP §2 "Oracle
  splits", because §0 admits only iverilog defects.
- ROADMAP §2:
  - 🆕 V: BLOCKED on the "Scoping" later-walk reads line, and on 🆕 AE
    for a decision it moves (Z1g; AE5–AE9 under a scope-wide pre-bind).
    The row records the mechanism and the three policies with their
    cells. Its oracles become iverilog + hand-IEEE.
  - New "Scoping" line (OPEN; iverilog + hand-IEEE): a later walk reads
    a later-declared generate parameter (N2 `K=8 bits=4 w=15`, B1, Q65
    `P=11 bits=3`, P1c, W2, Z0b `l2 X=2`, SN7 `P=9`; iverilog
    `K=4 bits=4 w=15`, `P=2 bits=3`, `l2 X=1`, `P=1`). With no outer
    object the read is accepted (Z5a–Z5d), and an override read steers
    a child's arm (DO02). Fix: restore each level's own keys at its
    entry in every walk after Nets; a decision it moves declines a run
    that reads a never-assigned 4-state variable.
  - 🆕 T stays BLOCKED on 🆕 U's held half and 🆕 V. It gains the
    unbound-label cells (Z5g undeclared; V14, V27, V30b, Z2c and Z3a
    declared later; all `def 9 bits=4` where iverilog refuses) and a
    note on its design: an unbound label must refuse, not take no match
    (round 3 reached this skip: R3q).
  - 🆕 AE now holds 🆕 V's moved decisions. "Oracle splits" gains the
    ruling line.
- ROADMAP §5.2: 🆕 V's row is removed. New order: 6 🆕 AI, 7 🆕 W with
  🆕 S (a)'s i64 half, 8 🆕 T then 🆕 S (a)'s wide half (now after
  🆕 U's held half and 🆕 V), 9 the "Size cast" enum lines, 10 the
  new-design census, 11 hygiene. The order prose and every
  `§5.2 row N` cite in docs/ follow.
- Summary recounted by line census: §2 start-order 37/9/28 ->
  37/8/29, §2 recorded 206/107/99 -> 208/108/100; total open
  475 -> 477, startable 276 -> 276, blocked 199 -> 201. `next` is now
  §2 1, 3, 4, 6–8 and 2, 9; §3.b 5; study/03 10.
- REMAINING_WORK §D: the 🆕 V line becomes the positional-binding
  prerequisite, which blocks 🆕 V and through it 🆕 T. The 4-state
  result channel also blocks 🆕 V. Row cites follow.
- PROBE_CATALOG, five new rows:
  - module-scope names are visible before their declaration (V01m,
    N2m, N2m2, Z5l);
  - §26.3 Example 1's variable form prints Z0a `px=0`, iverilog `px=1`;
  - a hierarchical label into a later block is skipped (V15);
  - a >64-bit select scrutinee is refused (Z3d2; 3 oracles
    `k 200 bits=8`);
  - a constant call in a generate region binds the `$unit` function
    (DF04 `@unit`; 3 oracles `@region`).
  E02 joins the §4.5.568 outer-object class. The §4.5.565 class and
  the §4.5.570 split are re-read under the ruling.
